title: Soft-pin coexistence strategy and testing lab notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a working strategy and lab-oriented test plan for running a soft-pin (coexistence) mode alongside strict region-pins. Goal is to allow staged adoption of hard pin enforcement without causing large-scale customer disruptions and to provide clear operator runbooks for detecting, diagnosing, and rolling back mis-routes.

Background / motivation:
- Customers ask for strict region pins (data never leaves region X) but operations show significant friction during initial cutovers (capacity imbalances, third-party geo-dependencies, config drift).
- Soft-pin coexistence = route preference + evidence capture, not absolute enforcement. Requests prefer local/anchored hosts but may fall back to a compatible remote region under constrained conditions.
- We need a reproducible lab and runbook so engineering, SRE, and solutions teams can validate customer migrations and avoid SLA regressions.

High-level strategy:
1) Policy model: prefer-local (soft pin) with explicit fallback gates
   - Prefer-local: requests for tenant T targeted to tenant-anchored region R when available.
   - Fallback gates (ordered):
     a) local-capacity-exhausted -> route to 'regional-failover-pool' in same geo (same continent)
     b) regional-pool-unavailable -> route to multi-region compatible pool with tenant consent flag (opt-in)
     c) emergency-operator-override -> route to nearest low-latency pool (captures evidence and escalates)
2) Evidence & auditable trail: every fallback must emit evidence packet (tenant_id, original_region, fallback_region, reason_code, KV-ttl snapshots) stored in residency-evidence-store for 90 days.
3) Customer-facing config surface: UI/API exposes mode=soft|strict and fallback_policy={same_continent, country_only, none}. Default to soft for new migrations.

Lab testbed topology (minimum reproducible environment):
- 3 region simulators: eu-west-1-mock, us-east-1-mock, ap-southeast-1-mock (network emulators to inject latency/loss).
- Tenant emulator that can toggle: anchor_region, consent_flag, traffic_profile (p95 seq length, burst pattern).
- Operator control plane mock (can inject node drain, put-region-into-maintenance, simulate per-pool quota exhaustion).
- Telemetry collector that aggregates residency-evidence and a separate store for request traces (zipkin-like).
- Canary harness that runs synthetic prompts and checks outputs & latencies.

Test matrix (examples):
- Normal steady-state: anchored region healthy -> expect 100% served locally, evidence entries show reason_code=LOCAL_OK. Verify latency and token-cost metrics.
- Local capacity saturation: simulate local GPU pool 95% utilized -> expect soft fallback to regional-pool, evidence reason_code=LOCAL_CAP_EXHAUST. Verify no more than 3% request failures, metric target: p95 latency increase < 2x baseline.
- Regional outage: shut down regional-pool -> expect fallback to multi-region pool only if consent_flag=true. If consent_flag=false, expect operator escalation and 503s with clear error body and evidence packet reason_code=REGION_UNAVAILABLE_NO_CONSENT.
- Degraded network: add high RTT to local region then validate preference still chooses local up to a latency threshold (configurable), and then triggers fallback when threshold breached.
- Rollout stress: gradually increase number of pinned tenants from 100 -> 10k with different traffic shapes; monitor routing thrash and telemetry ingestion rate.

Acceptance criteria for promoting from lab->staging:
- Evidence packets present and queryable for every fallback (test-run query < 5s).
- Test can produce deterministic rollback (operator toggles global-policy -> all tenants served from prior pool) and observe < 1 minute stabilization for routing tables.
- Canary metrics: request success rate >= 99% across scenarios, p95 latency within configured SLOs, and no silent data leaks (verify access logs and tenancy labels).

Operator runbook (quick commands & checks)
- Check current pin mode for tenant T: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" 
  https://control-plane/api/tenants/T/config -> expect field "pin_mode"
- Observe recent fallback evidence (last 60m): go to residency-evidence-store -> query tenant=T -> sort by timestamp
- If spikes of reason_code=LOCAL_CAP_EXHAUST: run 'rehydrate local pool' playbook (scale-up or drain low-priority workloads).
- If reason_code=CONSENT_REQUIRED: contact customer success; look up consent_flag via tenant API, and follow escalation template in linked artifacts.
- Emergency rollback: set control-plane feature flag 'force-strict-fallback-to-anchor=false' and 'global-routing-freeze=true' then monitor migrations-dashboard for stabilization.

Telemetry & alerts to add:
- Alert A: >1% requests for any tenant with pin_mode=strict observed with reason_code!=LOCAL_OK over 5m -> SEV2 (signals config drift).
- Alert B: Evidence store ingestion delay > 10s -> SEV3 (may lose auditability).
- Alert C: Fallback-rate across pinned-tenants > 0.5% sustained for 10m during promo -> Ops paging.
- Dashboard panels: per-tenant fallback-rate, fallback-reasons distribution, avg-latency-by-route, evidence-store-queue-depth.

Rollback & post-incident checklist:
- If a rollout causes unexpected hard fallbacks:
  1) Pause rollout (control-plane -> rollout.pause).
  2) Revert pin-mode for recently changed tenants to previous value.
  3) Re-run lab reproduction and collect traces.
  4) Open incident with annotation: "soft-pin-coexistence:rollback", attach evidence queries and canary run results.

Open design questions / tradeoffs (to discuss):
- Legal/audit: Is an evidence packet stored outside the anchored region for audit purposes acceptable? We currently include region metadata but need legal sign-off for cross-border evidence storage.
- Metrics cardinality: per-tenant telemetry may explode — do we sample or aggregate? Propose adaptive sampling: full evidence for tenants in migration cohorts, sampled for others.
- Consent UX: Should consent be explicit opt-in or implicit (with notice)? Product team input needed.
- Operator complexity: soft-pin increases observable states (preferred, fallback, consented). Can we present these as a single health score to operators?

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- (ENG) Build lab harness V1 with region simulators and simple tenant emulator (owner: Daniel). Target: staging-ready by 2026-01-30.
- (SRE) Add alerts A/B/C to staging monitoring (owner: Liam). Target: 2025-12-15.
- (Legal/Product) Decision meeting on evidence storage location and consent model. Schedule for 2025-12-01.
- (DX/SE) Draft customer-facing migration playbook and consent language (owner: Sofia). Target: 2026-01-10.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lab-first — we want to validate operational complexity before shipping UI primitives.
- The evidence packet schema is appended in the Confluence link (linked_artifacts). Please review compliance implications.
- Feedback requested: recommended sampling strategy for telemetry, operator UX simplifications, and acceptable SLO deltas during soft fallback windows.

Unresolved TODOs (short):
- Define exact TTL for evidence packets per territory (Legal).
- Add a runbook snippet for legal evidence export for audits.
- Benchmark evidence-store ingestion at 100k fallbacks/min.

---
Change log (high-level):
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-11-15: added test matrix and lab topology (Daniel)
- 2025-12-10: included operator commands and alerts (Liam)
- 2026-02-20: clarified fallback gates and acceptance criteria (Aisha)

End of note.
